discovery: Discovery of Bose-Einstein condensation of excitons in quantum Hall bilayers of two-dimensional electron systems

nominees.name: Allan H. MacDonald
nominees.affiliation: University of Texas at Austin, USA

subfield: Condensed matter physics (low-dimensional electron systems, many-body physics)
motivation: In closely spaced GaAs double quantum wells at total filling factor one, electrons in one layer bind to holes in the other and form a macroscopic coherent exciton condensate. MacDonald and co-workers predicted this interlayer phase coherence and its signatures. Eisenstein's experiments demonstrated them decisively: a Josephson-like resonant enhancement of interlayer tunnelling, quantized Hall drag, vanishing counterflow resistance showing dissipationless exciton transport, and a critical tunnelling current. These measurements depended on Pfeiffer's ultra-high-mobility MBE heterostructures and on precise independent contacts to each layer. Together they established the first unambiguous excitonic Bose condensate in a solid, a goal pursued for decades. The work led to today's exciton-condensate research in graphene and transition-metal dichalcogenide bilayers. It shows how carefully engineered materials, measurement craft and theory can bring out a new macroscopic quantum state.
